title: SML Mahindra rights issue: Price, record date and eligibility details - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
SML Mahindra’s ₹1,449.6-crore rights issue is priced at ₹3,506 per share, offering eligible shareholders a 36.3 per cent discount to Wednesday’s market price.

With SML shares rising nearly 4% to ₹5,549.30 on Wednesday, investors have just a trading sessions left to qualify for the ₹1,449.6 crore rights issue priced at ₹3,506 per share.

India’s commercial vehicle industry is seeing two distinct consolidation strategies: Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) is strengthening its domestic truck-and-bus presence through SML Mahindra, while Tata Motors is expanding globally through its acquisition of Italy’s Iveco.

Against this backdrop, SML Mahindra’s ₹1,449.6-crore rights issue offers eligible shareholders an opportunity to participate in the company’s next phase of growth. The issue is priced at ₹3,506 per share, representing a discount of about 37% to Wednesday’s market price of ₹5,549.30. The stock had touched an inter-day high of ₹5,600. Last two sessions since the announcement the stock price has jumped close to 9%.

Investors have only one trading sessions left to qualify for the rights entitlement, with November 20 fixed as the record date. Under the T+1 settlement cycle, November 19 is the last day to buy shares and become eligible for the two-for-seven rights issue.

“The commercial vehicle industry is witnessing two distinct approaches to consolidation. Mahindra-SML is bringing complementary truck-and-bus businesses together to strengthen its domestic competitive position, while Tata-Iveco is pursuing global scale, technology and access to international markets,” said automotive analyst Aveek Chattopadhyay.

Under the transaction, SML Mahindra will acquire Mahindra Truck and Bus Division (MTBD) for ₹525 crore. The business generated ₹2,989 crore in revenue in FY26, expanding the combined entity’s presence across buses, light, intermediate and heavy commercial vehicles.

M&M is targeting a rise in market share in India’s above-3.5-tonne commercial vehicle segment from around 6% currently to 10-12% by FY31 and more than 20% by FY36.

Beyond funding the MTBD acquisition, the rights issue will provide around ₹925 crore of additional financial capacity, before expenses and adjustments, to support manufacturing expansion, product development, alternative-fuel technologies and connected vehicle solutions.

Promoter M&M, which owns 58.97% of SML Mahindra, has committed around Rs 855 crore towards its entitlement and approved up to ₹595 crore for additional or unsubscribed shares.

While the steep discount may appear attractive, analysts caution that it does not automatically translate into gains.

“The discount makes the rights issue attractive at first glance, but investors should focus on earnings growth, capital allocation and the company’s ability to improve profitability after the integration,” said Kranthi Bathini, Director-Equity at WealthMills Securities.

For existing shareholders, the choice is whether to deploy additional capital behind M&M’s commercial vehicle ambitions or monetise their rights entitlements. Eligible investors who do not wish to subscribe can sell their rights entitlements on the exchange until December 4. The rights issue opens on December 1 and closes on December 9.
